thought: She lost her sight completely right before her board exams. She just became the first blind woman to argue a case before India's Supreme Court.
support: Anchal Bhateja was born with low vision due to retinopathy of prematurity, which progressively worsened until she lost her eyesight entirely just before her Class X board exams. She completed schooling using audiobooks, topped her Class XII exams, and qualified CLAT to become the first visually impaired student admitted to the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, graduating in 2023. On June 6, 2025, she became the first blind woman to argue a case before the Supreme Court of India, challenging a recruitment advertisement that excluded blindness from disability-reserved judicial service seats. She now works at Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy and mentors other blind law students.
